background_notes.fact: Here J_i={c∈C:c e_i∈M_R} is an R-submodule. Multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear bijection J_i→E_ii(M_R), and this image is finitely generated over R.

grounds.reason: R is embedded in C, so complex scalar multiplication restricts to R.
E_ii is the complex-linear coordinate projection associated with the supplied basis.
J_i is the inverse image of the identified R-submodule M_R under c↦c e_i.
The e_i form a complex basis, hence each e_i is nonzero.

background_notes.justification: Closure of M_R under addition and R-scalars gives the corresponding closure of J_i. The projection maps any vector to its i-th coordinate multiple and fixes every c e_i, proving the stated image equality. Since e_i≠0, c e_i=0 implies c=0. Writing vectors in a finite R-basis b_1,...,b_n shows that E_ii(b_1),...,E_ii(b_n) generate its image; the inverse scalar identification transports these generators to J_i.

background_notes.fact: For every w∈V, w=Σ_{i∈I}E_ii(w); for complex coefficients c_i, Σ_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0 implies c_i=0 for every i. Consequently, when J_i=J, the finite coordinate-sum map J^I→M_R is an R-linear isomorphism.

background_notes.justification: Expand w in the finite basis and apply each E_ii termwise; summing recovers w. Uniqueness of basis coefficients proves the asserted independence. Thus the coordinate-sum map lands in M_R, is onto by projection expansion, and has zero kernel by independence. Finite-sum distributivity proves R-linearity; a bijective linear map has linear inverse by applying its injectivity to addition and scalar multiplication.
